Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 1–4:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿The Most Merciful (1) taught the Quran (2) created man (3) taught him the explanation (4)﴾ [Ar-Rahman 1-4]. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and the clause ﴿taught the Quran﴾ is the predicate (khabar), ﴿created man﴾ is a second predicate, and ﴿taught him the explanation﴾ is a third predicate. The meaning is: this Great Lord, who named Himself ar-Rahman, has bestowed these blessings upon His servants. Ar-Rahman is the One possessing vast mercy, which encompasses everything, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [Al-A'raf 156].

He began this surah with ﴿ar-Rahman﴾ as a heading, indicating that everything that follows is from the mercy of Allah the Exalted and from His blessings. ﴿Taught the Quran﴾ — taught it to whom?! Taught it to Jibril? Taught it to Muhammad? Taught it to mankind?

The answer: He taught it to whomever He willed among His servants. He taught it first to Jibril, then Jibril descended with it upon the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ), second, then he conveyed it, Muhammad (ﷺ), to all people, third. The Quran is this noble Book which Allah the Exalted revealed in the Arabic language, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Quran that you might understand﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 3], and He the Exalted says: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (193) upon your heart that you may be among the warners (194) in clear Arabic language﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 193-195]. Teaching the Quran includes teaching its recitation (lafz), teaching its meaning, and teaching how to act upon it. Thus it comprises three things.

﴿Created man﴾, where the intended meaning is the species, so it includes Adam and his descendants; that is, He brought him into existence from nothing. Man was non-existent before his creation, before he was made. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ [Al-Insan 1]; meaning, there came upon him a period of time before he existed, when he was not a thing worth mentioning and was not known of. Allah the Exalted began with teaching the Quran before the creation of man, as an indication that Allah's blessing upon us in teaching the Quran is greater and more profound than His blessing in creating man. Otherwise, it is known that the creation of man precedes the teaching of the Quran; but since teaching the Quran is a greater favor from Allah the Mighty and Majestic upon the servant, He placed it before creation.

﴿Taught him the explanation﴾: taught whom? Taught man. ﴿Al-bayan﴾ means that by which one expresses what is in his heart. And ﴿taught him the explanation﴾ also means that by which something becomes clear during address. So here there are two kinds of bayan: the first bayan is from the speaker, and the second bayan is for the one addressed. The bayan from the speaker means expressing what is in his heart, which occurs by the tongue in speech, and occurs by the fingers in writing. When there is something in your heart that you want to inform someone of, sometimes you inform by speech, and sometimes by writing; both are included in His saying: ﴿taught him the explanation﴾.

Also, ﴿taught him the explanation﴾ means how a thing becomes clear. That, with respect to the listener, is that a person understands and knows what his companion says. And had Allah willed, He could have let the listener hear the sound without understanding the meaning, isn't that so?

So explanation, whether from the speaker or from the listener, is a favor from Allah the Mighty and Majestic. How great is this blessing? ﴿Taught the Quran (2), created man (3), taught him the explanation﴾ — three.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 5:

﴿The sun and the moon [move] by a precise reckoning.﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 5] Having spoken of the lower world, he now explains the upper world. ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by a precise reckoning.﴾ That is: by a precise calculation, they run as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded them. The sun and the moon have not changed since Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created them until He brings them to an end. They travel on one track, as Allah has commanded them. This is evidence of the perfection of Allah's power, the perfection of His dominion, and the perfection of His knowledge, that these great celestial bodies travel in an orderly motion and do not change over the long years.

So then: ﴿bi-husban﴾ ("by a precise reckoning") means: by a known calculation, perfectly executed and arranged with the utmost order.

﴿وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 6] ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate.﴾ (An-Najm) is an *ism jins* (a generic noun that refers to a whole class). What is meant is the stars: they prostrate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. These high stars that we see in the sky prostrate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a real prostration. However, we do not know its manner, because this is among the matters that minds cannot grasp. The tree prostrates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a real prostration, but we do not know how that is, as He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. There is not a thing except that it glorifies His praise, but you do not understand their glorification.﴾ [Al-Isra: 44].

So, an-najm: what is meant by it? That is, all the stars, all of them. Every tree on the earth prostrates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of mankind?﴾ [Al-Hajj: 18]. ﴿And many of mankind﴾ is contrasted with: ﴿and many deserve the punishment﴾ [Al-Hajj: 18], so they do not prostrate, may Allah protect us. ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of mankind, and many deserve the punishment?﴾

So: (an-najm) means the stars, (ash-shajar) means the trees. Do they prostrate literally or figuratively? Literally. They prostrate, but in what manner? Allah knows best; we do not know, and Allah is over all things capable.

Now look at the trees: when the sun rises, their leaves turn toward the sun, which you can see with your own eyes. And as it rises, the trees rise, and when it inclines toward setting, they incline too. This we observe, but this is not the prostration itself; the real prostration is not known.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 7:

﴿And the heaven He raised high﴾. That is: He raised the heaven. The Qur'an does not specify the extent of this elevation, but the Sunnah has come with regard to it. It is lofty and great, raised to a great and towering height.

﴿And He set up the balance﴾; that is, He established justice. The evidence that the meaning of "the balance" (al-mizan) here is justice is His, may He be blessed and exalted, saying: ﴿We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the balance﴾ [al-Hadid 25], meaning justice. The intended meaning of "the balance" here is not the well-known balance with two pans, no. The intended meaning of "the balance" is justice. The meaning of ﴿And He set up the balance﴾ [al-Rahman 7] is: He established it for the people so that they might uphold equity (al-qist), that is, justice.

Ibn 'Uthaymin, Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim, on Surah 55 (al-Rahman), verse 8:

﴿That you not transgress in the balance﴾ [al-Rahman: 8]. That is: that you not transgress in justice. The balance was set down so that you do not overstep in justice and thus act unjustly; you rule in favour of a person when he does not deserve it, or against a person when he does not deserve it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 55, verse 9:

﴿And establish the weight with justice﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 9]. ﴿الْوَزْنَ﴾ (al-wazn) means al-mawzun (the thing weighed), so "establish the weight" means: establish your weighing of things. Establish it and do not diminish it, so that you do not shortchange. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not make the balance deficient﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 9], meaning: do not make the thing weighed deficient. Thus al-mizan (the balance) differs in its three places. (Wada'a al-mizan) means what? 

* Students: Justice.

* The Shaykh: ﴿That you not transgress in the balance﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 8]: do not act unjustly in weighing. ﴿And establish the weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 9]: the thing weighed.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 10–13:

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures﴾ [Ar-Rahman 10]. That is, among the blessings of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is that Allah laid out the earth for the creatures (al-anam), meaning for the created beings.

﴿Therein is fruit, and palm trees with sheaths (akmam)﴾ [Ar-Rahman 11]; ﴿and grain with its husk, and fragrant plants﴾ [Ar-Rahman 12]; ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 13]. Allah laid the earth out for the creatures, meaning He made it low relative to the sky. Al-Anam are the creatures, like the two angels who are on the right and on the left, seated (qa'id), and the angels who guard by the command of Allah (al-mu'aqqibat), and the angels who descend on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), and others.

﴿Therein is fruit﴾, that is, on the earth there is fruit, meaning produce from which people enjoy (yatafakkahu) themselves, and the kinds of fruit are many, such as grapes, pomegranates, apples, oranges, and others.

﴿And the palm tree with sheaths﴾: He specified the palm tree because its fruit is the best of fruits, for it is sweets, sustenance, and fruit, and its tree is among the most blessed and most beneficial of trees. So much so that the Prophet (ﷺ) likened the believer to the palm tree, rather he likened it—that is, the palm tree—to the believer, saying: "Indeed among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is like that of the believer" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2209) and Muslim (2811/64), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar]. So the Companions began to guess about the tree until the Prophet (ﷺ) informed them that it was the palm tree.

His saying ﴿dhat al-akmam﴾: akmam is the plural of kimm, which is the covering of the fruit. When the palm's fruit first emerges, it has a strong kimm over it, then it grows within that kimm until it splits open and the fruit comes out.

﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plants﴾ [Ar-Rahman 12]: al-habb means that which is eaten, such as wheat, maize, millet, rice, and others.

His saying ﴿dhu al-'asf﴾: that is, what results from its stalk when it dries, which is known as straw (tibn), because it is crushed (yu'sif), meaning that livestock trample it with their feet until it is crushed.

﴿And the fragrant plants﴾: this is the tree with a pleasant scent. So Allah mentioned in the earth fruits, palm trees, grain, and fragrant plants, because each of these four has a distinct characteristic of its own, and all of that is for the benefit and advantage of the servants.

﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾: the address is to jinn and mankind, and the interrogative is for denunciation, meaning: which blessing of Allah will you deny?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 17–18:

﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 17] ﴿Lord﴾ here is the predicate of an omitted subject, and the meaning is: He is the Lord of the two easts and the Lord of the two wests. That is, He is their Owner and their Manager. Nothing rises except by the permission of Allah, and nothing sets except by the permission of Allah, and everything that the east and the west encompass belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He used the dual form "two easts" here with regard to the east of winter and the east of summer, because they differ. The sun in winter rises from the farthest south, and in summer it is the opposite. The moon, within a single month, rises from the farthest south and from the farthest north.

In another verse Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ [Al-Ma'arij: 40], using the plural. In a third verse: ﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no god but Him, so take Him as a Guardian﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9]. What is the reconciliation between them?

We say: As for the dual, it is with regard to the easts of winter and summer. As for ﴿the easts﴾ (plural), it is with regard to the rising point of each day and its setting point, because each day the sun rises from a place other than where it rose the day before, and likewise it sets; or with regard to the risers and the setters, since these include the sun, the moon and the stars, and none can count them except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So the plural is with regard to a rising point and setting point for each day, because each day differs from the next in its rising and setting; or with regard to the risers and setters, since they are many. Who counts the sun, the moon and the stars? None counts them except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

As for His saying: ﴿Lord of the east and the west﴾, it is with regard to the direction, because the directions are four: east, west, north and south. The plural here is easy and simple, with no difficulty. So we say: "the two easts" and "the two wests" — the dual is with regard to the west and east of winter and summer. The plural? It is with regard to the rising point of the sun each day and its setting each day, and this varies.

It is not hidden from you now how you find the sun's rising and setting changing each day, especially at the equinox: you find the difference of a minute or a minute and a half between its setting yesterday and today. Or it is with regard to the riser and setter, and the risers and setters are many, none can count them except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The singular is with regard to the direction, because the directions are four: east, west, north and south.

﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests (17). So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 17, 18] That is: which of the blessings of Allah will you two deny, O assembly of jinn and humankind? So what is our answer to these interrogations in all these verses? Our answer: "We deny none of Your favours, our Lord." For this reason a hadith is related, with a weakness in its chain, that when the Prophet ﷺ recited it to the Companions, they were listening to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) and did not respond with anything. So he said a statement whose meaning is: «Indeed the jinn were better in response than you; for whenever he recited a verse, they would say: "We deny nothing of Your favours, our Lord."»[[Narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad (5853) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.]] However, this hadith is weak; the commentators mention it here only.

What are the blessings and favours in the two easts and the two wests? Every verse that is followed by ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ includes great blessings. What blessings does the difference between east and west entail? Upon it depend the benefits of creation: summer and winter, spring and autumn, and other things we do not know. They are therefore great blessings in the difference of east and west.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 22–23:

﴿From both of them come forth the pearl and the coral.﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 22] ﴿From both of them﴾, meaning: from the two seas, the sweet and the salty. ﴿The pearl and the coral﴾, which are pieces of pearl, red, beautiful in shape and colour, even though they are (found in) water.

As for the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿from them﴾, He attributed the emergence to the two seas, the sweet and the salty. It has been said: the pearl only comes out of the salty (sea), and does not come out of the sweet (sea). Those who said this were confused about the meaning of the verse: how does Allah say ﴿from them﴾ when it is from only one of them? They answered: this is from the category of "taghlib" (predominance, where one side is given precedence over the other). Do you know taghlib? It is that one of the two sides dominates the other, as when it is said: "al-'Umarān" for Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and it is said: "al-Qamarān" for the sun and the moon. So this is from the category of taghlib, and so ﴿from them﴾ means one of them.

And some of them said: rather, this is by omission of a noun (ḥadhf al-muḍāf), and the implied meaning of ﴿from them﴾ is: from one of them.

So we have two opinions: either it is from the category of taghlib, or it is from the category of omitting the noun, the implied meaning being: it comes out from one of them.

There is a third opinion: that the verse remains on its apparent meaning, with no taghlib and no omission, and that ﴿from them﴾ means: from both of them together, the pearl and the coral, even though the salty (sea) is distinguished in being more abundant and finer.

So which of these three opinions do we take? We take what agrees with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. This is a rule you must understand: that we adopt what agrees with the apparent meaning. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿It comes out from both of them﴾, so who created them, and He knows what comes out of them? If the apparent meaning of the verse is that the pearl and the coral come out of both of them together, then it is obligatory to adopt its apparent meaning. Yet there is no doubt that the salty (sea) is more abundant and finer, but this does not prevent us from saying the apparent meaning of the verse; rather, it is necessary that we say the apparent meaning of the verse. This is a rule you should take from the Qur'an and the Sunnah: that we carry a matter upon its apparent meaning and do not interpret it, except in cases of necessity. If there is a necessity, we must proceed according to what the necessity requires. But without necessity, the Qur'an and the Sunnah must be carried upon their apparent meaning.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 23] Is this a continuation of the verse? Because what is in these seas, and the great benefits that arise from them, are numerous blessings that a human being can never deny.

﴿And His are the ships, elevated on the sea like mountains.﴾ [al-Rahman: 24].

﴿And His﴾ means: Allah's, the Mighty and Majestic, dominion, governance and facilitation.

They are a favour from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, like His favour upon His servants in the ships of the seas. For this reason He said: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 25], that is, which of Allah's blessings do you both deny? The address is to mankind and the jinn.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 29–30:

Then the Exalted and Glorified said: ﴿Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is in a matter.﴾ [Ar-Rahman 29] ﴿Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾, i.e., asks Allah. Those in the heavens are the angels, who ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Among their requests is that they seek forgiveness for those who believe, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾ to the end of the verse [Ghafir: 7]. And those on the earth among the creatures ask Him. The asking of the people of the earth of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is of two kinds:

The first: asking by the tongue of speech. This occurs only from the believers. The believer constantly asks his Lord for his needs, because he knows that none fulfills them except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. The believer's asking of his Lord is an act of worship; the asking itself is worship, whether or not your objective is achieved. So when you say, "O Lord, give me such-and-such," this is an act of worship, as the hadith states: "Supplication is worship" [Narrated by Abu Dawud (1479), at-Tirmidhi (2969), and Ibn Majah (3828) from the hadith of an-Nu'man ibn Bashir]. And the Almighty said, bearing witness to this hadith: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated﴾ [Ghafir: 60]. He said, "Call upon Me," then said, "Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me," and this is evidence that supplication is worship. This is supplication by the tongue of speech.

The second kind: supplication by the tongue of circumstance (lisan al-hal), which is that every creature is in need of Allah and looks to His mercy. For example, the disbelievers look at the rain descending from the sky, at the plants of the earth, at the health of animals, and at all sustenance, and they know that they cannot bring these things about by themselves. Thus they ask Allah by the tongue of circumstance. Therefore, when harm touches them and they are compelled to ask Allah by the tongue of speech, they ask Allah by the tongue of speech: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32].

So: ﴿Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾. Who are those in the heavens? The angels, and we have given you an example of their requests. Who are those on the earth? Mankind and the jinn. And asking, i.e., the asking of the people of the earth, is divided into two kinds: by the tongue of speech and by the tongue of circumstance.

﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾ [Ar-Rahman 29]. And who counts the days? No one except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. And who counts the affairs that occur in the days? No one except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾: He enriches a poor person and impoverishes a rich one, makes a healthy person ill and cures a sick one, grants security to one who fears and causes fear to one who is secure, and so on. Every day Allah, Exalted is He, does this. And are these changing affairs mere vanity, or are they for wisdom? The first or the second? The second: for wisdom, without doubt. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain?﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 115], and He said: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 36]. We believe that Allah does not decree a decree except for a wisdom; but we may know this wisdom and we may not know it. For this reason He said: ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾.

But know, O believer, that Allah, Exalted is He, does not decree for you a decree except that it is good for you. If harm befalls him, he is patient and awaits relief, and he says: "Constancy of a state is impossible," so he awaits relief, and it becomes good for him. If prosperity befalls him, he gives thanks, and it is good for him. This is not for anyone except the believer.

﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 30] We say about it what we said about the previous verses: the meaning is, "Which of the blessings of Allah do you deny?"

The answer: do we deny or not deny? We deny none of the blessings of Allah; rather we say: they are from Allah, so to Him be praise and to Him be thanks.

Whoever attributes a blessing to other than Allah is a denier? Yes, a denier, even if he does not say that he is a denier. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And you make your provision [to be] that you deny [it]﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 82]. This verse refers to their saying, "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star-setting (nawʾ)." The Prophet ﷺ, while speaking to his companions following a rain that had fallen, said to them after the dawn prayer: "Do you know what your Lord said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He said: 'Among My servants there have arisen those who believe in Me and those who disbelieve. As for the one who said: We have been given rain by the grace of Allah and His mercy, that one believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. And as for the one who said: We have been given rain by such-and-such a star-setting, that one disbelieves in Me and believes in the star.'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (846) and Muslim (71/125) from the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani.]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verses 33–36:

﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through. You will not pass except with authority.﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 33] After the warning, He said: if you are able to pass through what We intend for you, then pass through.

﴿to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth﴾ means: from their directions.

﴿then pass through﴾ but you are not able to do this. So the command here is one of incapacitation (ta'jiz). For this reason He said: ﴿You will not pass except with authority﴾, meaning: you have no authority. No one can pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth. Where would he go? To nothing. It is not possible.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 34] ﴿There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and [molten] brass, and you will not be defended﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 35], meaning: if you were able, or if you attempted it, this would be the punishment. ﴿A flame of fire and brass﴾ means: heated by fire. ﴿And you will not be defended﴾, meaning: none of you will help another. This verse is in the context of challenge (tahaddi, a direct challenge to those who cannot meet it). Whoever claims that it points to what scholars have reached through flight, so that they leave the earth's atmosphere and its gravity and reach, as they claim, the moon or beyond the moon, has made a grave error. The verse is clearly a challenge, and a challenge is the addressing of someone who is unable to do the thing.

Then we say: Have these people been able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens? Even if we suppose they have passed beyond the regions of the earth, they have not passed beyond the regions of the heavens. So it is clear that the verse is in the context of challenge, and that it does not point to what these people claim it points to. We say: a thing that has occurred is not something we deny. But affirming it does not require that the Qur'an or the Sunnah indicated it. The fact is a fact. They have left the earth's regions, but this would need proof, and it is a fact that requires no proof.

If you reflect on this verse in its context, you will find that this challenge is on the Day of Resurrection, because He said: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 26], then He mentioned: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and earth asks of Him﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 29], then He mentioned: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 33], then He mentioned what follows it concerning the Day of Resurrection.

﴿The criminals will be known by their marks, so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 41]; i.e., by their signs. They will be recognized by a sign, and among their signs—may Allah protect us—is that their faces will be black. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day when some faces will be whitened and some faces will be blackened.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 106]. Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 54–55:

﴿Reclining on couches whose linings are of brocade﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 54]; meaning: they enjoy this fruit while in the state of reclining. Accordingly, the word ﴿reclining﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the subject of the implied verb; that is, they enjoy or partake of fruit while reclining. As for reclining (al-ittika'), it is said that it means sitting cross-legged (at-tarabbu') and similar postures, because a person is most at ease when sitting cross-legged. It is also said that ﴿reclining﴾ means leaning on supports on the right, on the left and behind the back.

﴿On couches﴾; meaning: sitting on couches ﴿whose linings are of brocade﴾, meaning: the lining of the couch, which is what the couch is covered with ﴿of brocade﴾, which is thick silk brocade (dibaj). As for the upper surface of these couches, it is of sundus, which is thin silk brocade, and all of it is of silk.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens will be near at hand﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 54]. Reflect on or imagine this state! A person reclining, at peace and at rest, who wishes to partake of these fruits: does he get up from the place where he is settled and reclining in order to take the fruit? No. Allah explained this by His saying: ﴿And the fruit of the two gardens will be near at hand﴾. The scholars said: whenever he looks at a fruit and desires it, the branch bends down until the fruit is before him. He needs no exertion and no standing; rather he reclines, looking at the fruit with desire, and it hangs down to him by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, even though it is inanimate. But Allah has given it a sense by which it hangs down over him when he desires it. Do not be surprised by this now: most trees, in general, face the sun! Look at the faces of the leaves at the beginning of the day, and you will find them turned toward the east; at the end of the day they turn toward the west. There is a kind of awareness in them. Likewise: ﴿And the fruit of the two gardens will be near at hand﴾, close, so that when a man or a woman looks at it, it hangs down until it is before their hands.

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 55].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verses 74–75:

﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 74]. Meaning: no one has had intercourse with them; rather, they remain virgins until their husband approaches them when he enters Paradise. May Allah make us and you among them.

﴿Neither man has touched them﴾, ﴿nor jinn﴾, meaning: nor jinn. This indicates that jinn enter Paradise along with mankind, and so it is, because Allah does not wrong anyone. Among the jinn are the righteous and others below that; among them are Muslims and among them are qasiţūn (ﵟ, i.e., those who deviate), meaning disbelievers, just as with mankind. Just as among mankind there are the obedient and the disobedient, and among them the disbelieving and the believing, so too among the jinn.

The Muslim jinn is one of good, who points to good, gives tidings of good, and helps the people of righteousness among mankind. The jinn who is a sinner or a disbeliever is exactly like the sinner or disbeliever among the children of Adam. Their disbelievers enter the Fire by consensus, by the consensus of the Muslims, as in the Quran: ﴿He will say, "Enter into the company of nations who have passed away before you, of jinn and mankind, into the Fire"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38]. This is the explicit text of the Quran, and the scholars have unanimously agreed that the disbelieving jinn enter the Fire and the believing jinn enter Paradise. [Qur'an 55:76–77] Reclining on green cushions and fine rich carpets.

﴿Reclining﴾ means: leaning on their hands and backs.

﴿On cushions﴾ means: on cushions which quiver with a fluttering motion like the shilsh (is this known? The shilsh is found in cushions and beds; it is thus that it quivers), reclining on green cushions, because green is the most pleasing color to look at and the most delightful to the heart.

﴿And fine rich carpets﴾: the 'abqari (ʿabqarī) is the very finest of carpets, and for this reason everything excellent is called 'abqari. As the Prophet ﷺ said in the dream he saw when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) was drawing water: "I have not seen anyone like 'abqarī drawing water with such strength," meaning: he drew with the strength of his power, may Allah be pleased with him.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3682) and Muslim (2393/19), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar.]]

﴿And fine rich carpets﴾ [55:76]. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ [55:77] The meaning of this question is a affirmation: that the blessings are clear, so with what will you deny them?

The answer: we deny nothing. We acknowledge the favours of Allah, that is, His blessings, and we affirm them, and we acknowledge that we fall short and have not thanked Allah as He deserves. Yet we believe that Allah's forgiveness is wider than our sins, and that Allah, blessed and exalted, is Most Forgiving and Generous, who loves the repentance of His servant, loves those who repent, and loves those who purify themselves, to the point that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than any one of you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6309) and Muslim (2747/7), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]

Waiting for death; he had despaired of life once more. Then suddenly the halter of his camel was hanging on the tree, so he took it and said: "O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord!" What did he mean? He meant: You are my Lord and I am Your servant, but out of the intensity of his joy he made a mistake and said: "O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord." So Allah, the Exalted, is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than this man with his camel. O Allah, forgive us, O Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 55, verse 78:

﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Full of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 78] When He concluded the surah with this great sentence, meaning: how great is the blessing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and how great is the blessing in His name, to the point that the name of Allah makes a slaughtered animal lawful or unlawful. If a person slaughters an animal and does not say "in the name of Allah," what is it? It is carrion, unlawful, impure, harmful to the body. Even if he forgets, if he slaughters it and forgets to say "in the name of Allah," it is unlawful, impure, and corrupts the body, so it must be thrown to the dogs, because it is impure. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is grave disobedience﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. So observe the blessing. If a person performs wudu' and does not say "Bismillah," his wudu' is, according to some scholars, invalid, and he must repeat it, because the basmalah is obligatory according to some people of knowledge.

As for hunting: a person sees game, whether a crawling creature or a bird, shoots it, and does not say "Bismillah." What is this game? It is unlawful, carrion, impure, harmful to the body. So observe the blessing.

When a person comes to his wife, meaning he has intercourse with her, and says: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide for us," this is a protection for the child that may come from this intercourse, protecting him from Satan. The Prophet ﷺ said: "If one of you, when he approaches his wife, says: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You have provided for us,' and a child is decreed between them, Satan will never harm him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (141) and Muslim (1434 / 116), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas.]]

A person strives right and left to protect his child and spends large sums of money, and here is this remedy from the Messenger ﷺ. Is it expensive or cheap? It is cheap in terms of action, easy, and it protects him from Satan forever. All of this is evidence of the blessing of the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Full of Majesty and Honour﴾; i.e., Possessor of greatness ﴿and Honour﴾. Is "Honour" meaning that He is honoured or that He honours? Both: He is honoured, respected and magnified, the Mighty and Majestic, and He also honours. Allah the Exalted said concerning the people of Paradise, may Allah make us among them: ﴿Those will be in gardens, honoured﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 35]. So He is Possessor of Majesty and Honour, He honours whoever deserves honour, and He honours His righteous servants, may Allah make us and you among them by His grace and generosity.

And here our reading of Surat al-Rahman comes to an end.
